subject: Partial regional disruption (APAC) — automated switch & verification steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: [SRE] APAC: targeted egress peering degradation — short note

Quick summary: starting ~15:45 UTC we observed elevated SYN retries and increased tail latency for a subset of APAC egress nodes servicing GCP ap-southeast1. Error rate peaked at ~6% for HTTP/1.1 POSTs to model endpoints. Root cause appears to be an upstream peering flap combined with a local router hardware queueing misconfiguration. Traffic is still admitting but degraded.

Immediate mitigation applied: we disabled the affected peering path and started automated reroute to backup peering (apac-sidecar-2). Traffic is flowing to the fallback path, but some customers with pinned region=apac and strict affinity may see request retries or small failovers.

Action items for ops:
- Confirm fallback path health and slow drain the KV caches to refresh connections (I kicked the cache-refresh job).
- Prepare a customer-facing note and include step-by-step verification and an MFA-friendly checklist.
- Attach logs slice to the incident.

I'll hand off to Rishi for external comms. ETA for full remediation: 4-6 hours pending hardware replacement; we'll update if timelines change.

--
Diego Fernandez
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sre-log-slice-apac-08-22.txt (text, 120KB)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@saasco.com>, ops@saasco.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: APAC service degradation — guidance to validate automated switch (Action required)

Hi Emily / SaaSCo ops team —

Short version: We detected a targeted network degradation impacting a subset of APAC egress peering (ap-southeast1). We have activated an automated reroute to our backup peering, which should preserve request paths for most traffic. Because your integration pins region=apac and uses short-lived KV affinities, we want to make sure your production traffic is unaffected end-to-end.

What we (Redwood) have done already:
- Automated traffic reroute to apac-sidecar-2; prefix caching restarted.
- Scoped mitigation to affected peering; unrelated regions (US / EU) are not impacted.
- Opened INC-2027-4623 and attached logs for your account. Link: https://redwood.app/incident/INC-2027-4623

What we ask you to verify (quick checklist):
1) Confirm your service is observing model responses within acceptable latency (p50/p95). If you use our SDK, run: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-2","input":"ping"}' and include X-Request-Id.
2) If you maintain IP whitelists tied to the APAC egress CIDRs, please allow the fallback range 34.210.112.0/20 for the next 6 hours.
3) If you see 5xx spikes or persistent timeouts, flag here with sample request IDs and timestamps and we will prioritize session-affinity fixes.

Attached 'reroute-quicksteps.pdf' has step-by-step checks for customers that maintain strict egress ACLs. I've also added a mutual-action-plan spreadsheet (MMP) for tracking any procurement or network changes should you elect to change routing preferences long-term.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 15-minute bridge — I recommend looping Tom Nguyen from Marketplace (cc'ed on the next message) if your deployment uses cloud marketplace-provisioned networking.

I'll post updates to this thread as we confirm remediation.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: reroute-quicksteps.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: INC-2027-4623 post-incident update + short postmortem draft

Emily / SaaSCo ops team —

Thanks for the sample IDs; I correlated them to the peering flap and can confirm the following timeline:
- 15:44:27 UTC: initial peering instability observed (packet drops + SYN retries).
- 15:46:10 UTC: automated reroute initiated to apac-sidecar-2.
- 15:46:10–15:51:00 UTC: we observed retries for sessions pinned to the original egress; two SaaSCo requests show 503 then successful retry within ~14s after reroute.

Root cause: controller failed to gracefully drain a small set of router hardware queues during a peering flap; this caused brief head-of-line blocking and timeouts for affinity-bound sockets. The hardware vendor will replace the queued line card; we expect closure by 2027-08-26 pending parts.

Customer impact: Short-lived (<=1 minute for most requests, up to ~14s for the two sample IDs) transient 503s during the reroute window. No data loss, all requests ultimately processed.

Remediations & follow-ups we are taking:
- Hardware replacement (vendor) for affected router card.
- Controller patch to ensure graceful queue drain during reroute (backport patch scheduled for next release).
- Add explicit instrumentation to map session-affinity transitions for affected peering paths.

Attached is a short postmortem draft and the mutual action plan (MMP) with suggested communication and any SLA considerations. We have flagged the event for potential goodwill credit consideration; Ben, please advise whether we should proactively offer a small credit for the window.

I'll keep this thread open and publish the finalized postmortem to the incident drive link once Ben and Product OK the wording.

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: postincident-summary-draft.md (markdown, 6KB)]
